title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
spaceBreakdown:
- int lo, hi, mid: constant number of scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no auxiliary allocations
- not counted: input vector `nums`, returned bool
approach: Use binary search, but handle the ambiguity duplicates create. Normally, comparing `nums[mid]` with `nums[lo]` tells you which half is sorted; with duplicates, when `nums[lo] == nums[mid] == nums[hi]` you cannot tell, so shrink both ends by one and continue. Otherwise, identify the sorted half and check whether `target` lies inside its range to decide which half to keep. This is correct because at least one half is always sorted in a rotated sorted array, and the shrink step guarantees progress even in the fully-ambiguous case.
hints: The array is two sorted segments joined end-to-end. Pick any middle position - what must be true about at least one of the two halves on either side of it?

Binary search. In `[2,5,6,0,0,1,2]` with `target=0`, `mid=3` gives `nums[mid]=0` - found. Otherwise compare `nums[mid]` with `nums[lo]` and `nums[hi]` to find the sorted half; when all three are equal, shrink both ends.

```
lo, hi = 0, n-1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
    if nums[mid] == target: return true
    if nums[lo] == nums[mid] == nums[hi]:
        lo += 1; hi -= 1
    else if nums[lo] <= nums[mid]:
        if nums[lo] <= target < nums[mid]: hi = mid - 1
        else: lo = mid + 1
    else:
        if nums[mid] < target <= nums[hi]: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid - 1
return false
```

**All equal, target absent** - every element identical, target not among them
`Input: nums = [1,1,1,1,1], target = 2` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the `nums[lo]==nums[mid]==nums[hi]` check and using `nums[lo]<=nums[mid]` to declare left sorted → infinite loop (lo and hi never converge past the equal run)

**Single element** - array of length 1
`Input: nums = [5], target = 5` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using `while lo < hi` instead of `while lo <= hi` → returns false without checking the only element

**Target at both ends** - target equals `nums[0]` and `nums[n-1]` after rotation
`Input: nums = [2,5,6,0,0,1,2], target = 2` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using strict `nums[lo] < target` instead of `nums[lo] <= target` in the left-half check → misses target at index 0, returns false

**Duplicates hiding the pivot** - equal values straddle the rotation boundary
`Input: nums = [1,3,1,1,1], target = 3` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: treating `nums[lo]<=nums[mid]` as "left sorted" without first excluding the all-equal case → walks lo past index 1 (where 3 lives), returns false

followUps.q: What if you must return an index where target occurs, not just true/false?
followUps.a: Return `mid` as soon as `nums[mid]==target`; the same binary search works unchanged. If you need the first or last occurrence among duplicates, after a match linearly scan left/right through equal neighbors, degrading to O(n) worst case, O(log n) average, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if you must also find the rotation pivot k?
followUps.a: Locate the index of the minimum element via binary search with the same all-equal shrink step; that index is k. O(n) worst case, O(log n) average, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if nums arrives as a forward-only stream too large to store?
followUps.a: Binary search needs random access, so it cannot apply. Fall back to a single linear scan comparing each streamed element to target - O(n) time, O(1) space, one pass.
